findings.title: Fixed-mode budgets show split as override
findings.problem: _displayed_member_max_budget treats allocation_mode == "fixed" as "this member has a saved override". That does not hold for a budget created in fixed mode: ProjectBudgetCreateRequest.allocation_mode is a free string, _validate_allocation_mode accepts any AllocationMode value including "fixed", and create_project_budget passes it to _allocate_equal (project_budget_service.py:925-932), which stamps every member row with that mode. On such a budget, with enforcement off, never-overridden members now return their equal-split share instead of budget.max_budget, and allocated_member_budget_total falls to the sum of those shares.
findings.impact: Reachable from the create endpoint (verified against source). For budgets created in fixed mode the change alters the displayed amount for members who have no override — the population the task says must keep returning budget.max_budget — while the task also states the rule as "allocation_mode is fixed". Display only; nothing enforced at the provider changes.
findings.recommendation: Human decision required: for a budget created with allocation_mode="fixed", should never-overridden members display their stored share (the task's literal "allocation_mode is fixed" rule — no code change) or budget.max_budget (the task's "non-overridden members keep returning budget.max_budget")? If the latter, discriminate in the router on the override itself — `allocation.override_budget_id is not None`, set at project_budget_service.py:1472 and cleared at :1542 — instead of on allocation_mode, and add a regression test for a fixed-mode budget with no overrides. Keep the change inside project_budget_router.py: src/codemie/service/budget/ is out of scope for this task. Gating on the assignment's mode instead would hide real overrides on fixed-mode budgets.
